states.changed: A visitor meets seventeen written instructions of this house that a script can decide from Git, read against the full public history of its four repositories: one lane per instruction and practice, one cell per day opening to each file and commit, and reads that 171 of 8,098 bound items broke a limit, none a prohibition or a duty, and that only 39 break a limit in every reading of what a line and a word are.

A visitor now meets who saw first: one mark per broken limit, placed by the day it was committed and the days until anyone named it in writing, and reads that 8 of the 171 were named before the census, each by the practice that broke the rule, while the rest sit on the census line after a median of 28 days; then the architect's own record, one square per deed of the house's machines beyond or against their instructions in the site's decision log, grouped by who saw it first: the architect 13 and a session he set to look 9 of the 29 rows that say, the machines unbidden 7, nobody outside the house; each mark and square opens to its commit or its row.

A visitor now meets the check: the limits struck before the census put back, 129 breaches of which 78 were named before it, each by the practice that broke the rule, so that the rules seen to break turn out to be the ones that were struck; the decision log coded a second time, blind, with its agreement, now 88 deeds of which 6 are acts of authority, each square ringed in red and opening to its commits; and each deed found at its commit, 80 of 88, of which only 12 show in Git alone that a machine did it, while 69 carry the architect's name. The census is corrected by the Atelier's offer to 156 of 8,073.

A visitor now meets the paper: the six acts of authority in one table, each with its commit, the name Git gives it, who saw it first and the commit that mended it, and reads that every one of the five found in Git was mended under the architect's name in a commit that does not name what it mends; then every deed joined to its mending from Git alone, 75 of 77 mended under his name, the median within 3.5 days, 1 of the 70 separate mendings naming the commit it mends; the Atelier's correction of 21 November read against the items, which holds and changes no count; the five current studies the paper stands beside, each with the passage it is read for.
